content: The Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) provides expert advice and guidance on the effective prevention and control of vaccine-preventable diseases. This includes specific recommendations for special populations that may require modifications to standard vaccination guidelines. One such population is pregnant and breastfeeding women. Developing vaccination recommendations for pregnant and breastfeeding women is particularly challenging due to the limited availability of scientific evidence necessary to inform these decisions. To address this, the ACIP Workgroup on Vaccines during Pregnancy and Breastfeeding was established in 2007. The purpose of this workgroup was to create guiding principles for drafting ACIP recommendations specific to this population. The workgroup included ACIP members, representatives from professional medical organizations, subject matter experts, and consultants from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Between April 2007 and March 2008, the workgroup conducted a thorough review of existing policies regarding vaccine use in pregnant and breastfeeding women. Based on this review, along with input from workgroup members and feedback from partner organizations, the workgroup developed a document titled Guiding Principles for Development of ACIP Recommendations for Vaccination during Pregnancy and Breastfeeding. This document was approved by ACIP in March 2008. The guiding principles outlined in this document aim to standardize the process for policy formulation and ensure consistency in presenting the rationale and recommendations for vaccination in pregnant and breastfeeding women. Key topics addressed in the document include: 1. Guidance on structuring the background section of recommendations. 2. Recommendations for the structure and language used in vaccination guidelines. 3. Clarification of the definitions of precautions and contraindications in the context of pregnancy and breastfeeding. 4. Suggestions for decision-making approaches when adequate data are unavailable. 5. A description of a consistent process for gathering expert opinions. These principles are intended to be applied to future ACIP vaccine statements and updates to existing statements that consider vaccination in pregnant and breastfeeding women.
